prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1205; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a sideswipe that occurred while the insured was changing lanes. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will be routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy file and confirmed the driver involved is a named driver on the policy. Coverage was in force at the time of the loss, and nothing in the file suggests the vehicle damage predates the policy start.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report and statements from two witnesses. Both confirm the collision happened as described and that the claimant was in the vehicle at the time. Scene photos and the other driver's account match the same sequence of events.

Entry 4: Inspected the vehicle damage. The pattern and location are consistent with the described side impact, and no earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior claims or repair records.

Entry 5: Counsel submitted the medical file reporting a knee injury. The injury is plausible for a collision of this type. The claimant's account has been consistent across every conversation so far. Records also show a minor strain to the same area years ago that healed fully.

Entry 6: Treatment followed a typical course and tapered as the claimant improved. Based on the records and the matching vehicle damage, the injury appears related to this loss, and the file is moving to evaluation.
